A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Inheritune research despite the changed title and organization. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2 training, initialization ablations, downstream evaluations, and low-data OpenLLaMA experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original training results and adds experiments including GPT-2 Small layer transfer and LLaMA-3 attention-head analysis.

M1.justification: The operational recipe remains early-layer inheritance, copying embeddings and the prediction head, retraining, and progressive growth. v3 characterizes useful layers through AvgRank, but Section 4 retains the same half-depth initialization and two-layer increments; a different selection procedure is not established.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated C4 evaluation for LLaMA-3 attention analysis and tests OpenWebText-trained GPT-2 models on held-out FineWeb_edu data, introducing a distribution-shift scenario. Wikitext evaluation disappears. The principal training corpora and most downstream task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The new GPT-2 Small transfer comparison adds middle-block initialization alongside early-block, lazy-block, and random initialization (Figure 2 and Table 4). The stacking, hybrid-stacking, half-width, distillation, and low-data language-model comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a four-layer GPT-2 Small comparison trained for 100K steps and head-level LLaMA-3 evaluation, while dropping the reported 200K-step controls. Section 2 also changes the stated rank aggregation from averaging sequence-wise maxima to maximizing head-wise averages; this does not establish that reused plots were recomputed.

E4.justification: The attention-collapse investigation expands substantially: v3 tests early versus middle versus late layer transfer, cross-dataset robustness, OpenLLaMA mass concentration, and LLaMA-3 head collapse. It also adds GPT-2 xLarge attention visualizations and an Inheritune rank-mitigation comparison. Existing submodule and low-data ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The attention analyses retain the established sampling and averaging practice, including 100 sampled sequences and variability displays; existing attention-map averages over three samples remain. Neither version introduces training-seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: New results include GPT-2 Small validation losses of 3.25, 3.22, 3.19, and 3.23 for random, early, middle, and late initialization, and approximately 500 of 1024 LLaMA-3 heads exhibiting collapse. v3 removes v2 Table 1's OpenWebText-model downstream scores and 200K-step losses, including the xLarge baseline's 2.62 versus Inheritune's 2.64. Retained benchmark table values are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 revises the mathematical definition of rank aggregation by reversing the averaging and maximization order and introduces the block-level AvgRank statistic. The underlying 90% SVD and column-mass criteria remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion qualify collapse as frequent, near-rank-one behavior, and the abstract drops v2's categorical assertion that affected layers cannot learn anything meaningful. The central contributions—identifying lazy layers and producing smaller models with comparable performance through Inheritune—remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets transfer quality through layer rank rather than proximity to embeddings, distinguishes attention sinks from entirely lazy layers, and acknowledges that LLaMA-3 may contain many collapsed heads without whole lazy layers. These add meaningful mechanism explanations and an applicability qualification.

D1.justification: v3 drops v2's identification of FineWeb_edu as a 100B-token dataset and its deduplication/filtering description, reducing dataset documentation without establishing a changed dataset. The code link, optimizer settings, hardware, and detailed training hyperparameters are retained in the relocated implementation appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citation of Xiao et al.'s attention-sink work, plus C4 and RedPajama references. The Wikitext-related Merity reference and LLaMA 2 reference disappear. The broader positioning against rank-collapse research and existing training recipes remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract and conclusion, reorganizes the attention-collapse discussion, and integrates the separate training-without-repetition section into the experiments. Baseline descriptions and attention visualizations move into a substantially reorganized appendix structure.

P2.justification: v2's six-panel Figure 1 is split across rank, mass, and transfer displays. v3 adds a method schematic and several diagnostic figures, combines FineWeb training curves with an average-performance table, and moves the trimmed main results table into the appendix. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the central diagnosis through the middle-layer control, cross-dataset checks, modern-model analyses, and clearer applicability qualifications. However, it removes downstream evidence and longer-training controls, including the xLarge baseline that outperformed Inheritune, while retaining broad superiority claims. The stronger diagnostic support and reduced comparative completeness create material tradeoffs without a reliably assessable net direction.
